findings.notes: Every one of the five reported ANOVA F values tested falls outside the interval reachable from the paper's own printed means and SDs, with a Monte Carlo exact-match rate of 0 across 5,000 draws of the rounding box. The direction is NOT consistent: four reported F values are smaller than achievable and one (SS-QOL total, 21.217 vs 18.12-18.16) is larger, which argues against a single benign explanation such as the authors having run a repeated-measures rather than a one-way ANOVA -- removing within-subject error would raise F systematically, not lower it in four cases out of five. Two caveats. First, the recomputation treats the tabulated dispersions as SDs; Table II explicitly labels its dispersion 'SEM', and under the SEM reading the Barthel F would be roughly 0.5, still nowhere near 4.766, so that row fails under either reading. Tables IV and V carry no SD/SEM label at all. Second, three of the five means feeding the FIM recomputation are themselves GRIM-impossible, so for those the inputs are already in question. The paper reports 24 such F values in total and none carries degrees of freedom.

findings.title: Between group p values match uncorrected tests
findings.description: Both between-group p-values reproduce from the Table V means and SDs as ordinary two-sample t-tests. But the Methods state 'ANOVA with a post-hoc analysis (Bonferroni)', and these values match the UNCORRECTED comparison: with three pairwise group contrasts, a Bonferroni-adjusted p for the SS-QOL total would be roughly three times 0.039, i.e. about 0.12, and would not be significant. So the numbers are arithmetically consistent but appear not to carry the correction the Methods claim. Recorded as `consistent` because that is what the recomputation shows; the correction discrepancy is an interpretive point for the editorial stage.

findings.title: No duplicated summary statistics
findings.description: 1,728 cross-group (mean, SD) comparisons produced no identical pairs. Blocks were defined per GROUP rather than per table, because the three groups are genuinely different participants while the three tables describe the same people measured on different instruments -- comparing tables against each other would have flagged legitimate within-person repetition. A few isolated SDs recur across groups (12.12, 11.47, 11.91) but no mean/SD PAIR does, which is unremarkable at two decimal places. findings.title: Power analysis not reproducible (Methods, Statistical analysis)
findings.description: The calculation cannot be reproduced because no effect size is stated -- a reporting gap, not evidence the calculation is wrong. There is a separate and more substantive problem the tool cannot see: the formula the paper actually prints, n = N*X/(X + N - 1) with X = Z^2(alpha/2)*p(1-p)/MOE^2, is a formula for estimating a PROPORTION in a finite population with a given margin of error. It contains no power term at all, so it cannot deliver '1-beta = 0.80', and the paper states neither p, nor MOE, nor the population size N that it requires. That the required N (>= 70) exactly equals the N recruited (70) is also worth a reader's attention.

findings.title: No test statistics machine readable (Whole Results section)
findings.description: statcheck extracted zero test statistics from the complete Results text. This is not a tool failure: the paper reports all 24 ANOVA F values in the form 'F = 10.840, p < 0.001', with no degrees of freedom anywhere in the article. findings.title: Multiplicity tool refused
findings.description: multiplicity_report returned n_tests = 0 on three attempts, with and without an explicit `correction_applied` field and with `p_is_threshold` supplied, so the intended arithmetic was never performed. Recording the refusal rather than substituting hand arithmetic. What could not be quantified: the paper runs 24 omnibus ANOVAs plus roughly 60 post-hoc and between-group comparisons across four instruments on the same 70 patients, and states a Bonferroni correction only within each ANOVA -- never across outcomes or across the three group contrasts. The uncorrected multiplicity burden is therefore substantial but is left unquantified here.
